newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur barges slip, cargo market lifeles.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur barges slip, cargo market lifeles.

text.p: NWE high sulphur barge prices slipped on Thursday with little business done on most fuel oil markets ahead of the Easter weekend.

After Wednesday's price jump to $89 fob ARA, trading began on Thursday at $88 before slipping lower. Large volumes were moved at $86 fob ARA by one aggressive seller. Swaps were off a dollar at $86/$87 for April.
There was little bunker interest with most needs for the long Easter weekend already met.
Traders pegged afternoon levels at $87 to sell and $86 to buy but expected little activity.
"I think people will be going home early before the weekend," said one seller.
Cargo markets were lifeless, becalmed by the approach of the long weekend.
"Prices are stable because noone is moving them one way or another," said one trader.
Fresh statistics on exports of Russian heavy fuel showed a significant year on year increase.
Exports from the Baltic and Black Sea ports rose 61,723 bpd from last week and were 173,426 bpd higher than in the same last year, according to figures from Geneva-based consultancy Petro-Logisitics.
